description: Plain, free, no-paid-API HTTP/sitemap-based web crawler for RAG pipelines. Set `sitemap_url` to follow a sitemap.xml (or sitemap index) exhaustively, or `start_urls` to breadth-first crawl from one or more seed pages following same-domain links up to `max_pages`/`max_depth`. Respects robots.txt by default. Output rows are ready to feed into document_chunker for a RAG pipeline.
summary: Crawl a site via sitemap.xml or same-domain link-following, no API key required, ready for RAG pipelines.
name: Sitemap Crawler Ingestion

outputs.description: pandas DataFrame with one row per crawled page (or MaterializeResult if destination is non-SQL / persist_only=true).

asset_name.label: Asset Name
asset_name.description: Name of the asset that will hold the data

sitemap_url.label: Sitemap Url
sitemap_url.description: URL of a sitemap.xml (leaf <urlset>, or a <sitemapindex> listing child sitemaps -- followed one level deep) to crawl exhaustively. Every <loc> URL is fetched; max_pages/max_depth do not apply. Required unless start_urls is set (exactly one of the two, not both, not neither).

start_urls.label: Start Urls
start_urls.description: Comma-separated seed URL(s) to crawl breadth-first, following same-domain <a href> links up to max_pages/max_depth. Required unless sitemap_url is set.

max_pages.label: Max Pages
max_pages.description: Max total pages to fetch in plain-crawl mode (start_urls). Ignored (with a logged warning if left non-default) when sitemap_url is set -- a sitemap declares its own complete URL list.

max_depth.label: Max Depth
max_depth.description: Max link-following hops from the nearest seed URL in plain-crawl mode (start_urls). Ignored (with a logged warning if left non-default) when sitemap_url is set.

include_patterns.label: Include Patterns
include_patterns.description: Comma-separated substrings (not regexes -- see component docstring for why) a candidate URL must contain at least one of, to be fetched. Applied in both modes, e.g. '/docs/' to scope a crawl or sitemap to one section of a site.

exclude_patterns.label: Exclude Patterns
exclude_patterns.description: Comma-separated substrings; a candidate URL containing any of these is skipped. Applied after include_patterns, in both modes.

respect_robots_txt.label: Respect Robots Txt
respect_robots_txt.description: Check each domain's robots.txt (via urllib.robotparser) before fetching any page, skipping disallowed URLs. Set False only when you have explicit permission to crawl a site regardless of its robots.txt.

request_delay_seconds.label: Request Delay Seconds
request_delay_seconds.description: Seconds to sleep between successive page fetches -- politeness, avoid hammering a site.

user_agent.label: User Agent
user_agent.description: User-Agent header sent with every request. Defaults to a string identifying this project (not a browser impersonation) -- change it to identify your own deployment if a site's robots.txt or access logs need that.

hash_columns.label: Hash Columns
hash_columns.description: Column names to pseudonymize (salted SHA-256, hex-encoded) before the data reaches the destination -- same deterministic-hashing pattern dlt's own docs recommend for PII (https://dlthub.com/docs/general-usage/customising-pipelines/pseudonymizing_columns). A column missing from a given row is skipped, not an error. Requires hash_salt or hash_salt_env_var.

hash_salt.label: Hash Salt
hash_salt.description: Salt for hash_columns. Required (this or hash_salt_env_var) when hash_columns is set -- a hardcoded/shared salt would let the hash be reversed by dictionary attack on common values. Use "{{ env.VAR_NAME }}" for the inline form. Keep it stable across runs: changing it changes every hash.

hash_salt_env_var.label: Hash Salt Env Var
hash_salt_env_var.description: Alternative to hash_salt: name of an env var holding the salt. Resolved at run-time.

on_schema_change.label: On Schema Change
on_schema_change.description: What to do when incoming data's shape differs from the destination table's established schema (new columns, or a column's data type changing). 'allow_all' (default, today's behavior): accept any change. 'allow_new_columns': accept new columns, but reject (fail the run) a column whose data type would change. 'block_all': reject both new columns and data type changes. The first materialization can always create its initial schema in every mode -- 'block_all' only locks down an ALREADY-established table's columns/types. A rejected change fails the run with a clear error naming the table and column -- it is never silently dropped.

exclude_columns.label: Exclude Columns
exclude_columns.description: Column names to drop from every row before it reaches the destination. Applied before hash_columns (so a column in both ends up excluded, not hashed-then-excluded). A column missing from a given row is skipped, not an error, matching hash_columns.

max_rows_per_resource.label: Max Rows Per Resource
max_rows_per_resource.description: Caps how many crawled-page rows load into the destination. Unset (default): no cap. This still loads real rows into the real destination -- it is not a dry run or a preview -- meant for a first run to check a connection and the shape of the data cheaply, not for routine use. Never applied unless you set it.

destination.label: Destination
destination.description: dlt destination identifier (e.g. 'snowflake', 'bigquery', 'postgres', 'redshift', 'filesystem', 'duckdb', 'databricks', 'athena', 'clickhouse', 'mssql', 'motherduck'). Leave empty for in-memory DuckDB -> DataFrame mode.

dataset_name.label: Dataset Name
dataset_name.description: Target dataset/schema in the destination. Defaults to the asset name.

persist_only.label: Persist Only
persist_only.description: If True with destination set: emit a MaterializeResult and skip DataFrame return. If False: query the destination back into a DataFrame (only meaningful for SQL destinations -- non-SQL destinations always emit MaterializeResult).

destination_credentials_url.label: Destination Credentials Url
destination_credentials_url.description: Inline connection string passed to dlt's destination factory. Useful when one Dagster project ingests into multiple accounts of the same destination type. If unset, dlt resolves credentials from env vars -- see ../DESTINATIONS.md.

destination_credentials_env_var.label: Destination Credentials Env Var
destination_credentials_env_var.description: Alternative to destination_credentials_url: name of an env var holding the connection string. Resolved at run-time.

bucket_url.label: Bucket Url
bucket_url.description: Bucket/path URL for filesystem-shaped storage (e.g. 's3://my-bucket/path', 'gs://my-bucket/path', 'az://my-container/path', or 'file:///local/path'). Required when destination='filesystem' (the final write target). Also used as the staging area when destination='databricks' or 'athena', both of which require an intermediate filesystem stage before the warehouse-side load -- dlt resolves the bucket's credentials from the destination-appropriate standard environment variables (e.g. AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY) unless destination_credentials_url/destination_credentials_env_var is set.

athena_query_result_bucket.label: Athena Query Result Bucket
athena_query_result_bucket.description: Optional S3 path where Athena writes query results (e.g. 's3://my-bucket/results/'). Only used when destination='athena'. May be omitted to use Athena-managed query results instead.

owners.description: Asset owners — team names (team:analytics) or email addresses.
owners.label: Owners

asset_tags.description: Key-value tags applied to the asset in the Dagster catalog, e.g. {"domain": "finance"}.
asset_tags.label: Asset Tags

kinds.description: Asset kinds shown in the Dagster catalog (e.g. snowflake, python). Auto-inferred from component name if empty.
kinds.label: Kinds

freshness_max_lag_minutes.description: Maximum acceptable lag in minutes before this asset is considered stale.
freshness_max_lag_minutes.label: Freshness Max Lag (minutes)

freshness_cron.description: Cron schedule for the freshness policy, e.g. '0 9 * * 1-5' (weekdays 9am).
freshness_cron.label: Freshness Cron Schedule

include_preview_metadata.label: Include Preview Metadata
include_preview_metadata.description: Include sample data preview in metadata

preview_rows.label: Preview Rows
preview_rows.description: Rows to include in the preview metadata when `include_preview_metadata` is True. For long DataFrames (>10x preview_rows), a random sample is used so the preview reflects the data distribution; otherwise head() is used.

deps.description: Lineage-only upstream asset keys (no data passed at runtime).
deps.label: Deps

partition_type.description: Enable partitioning: 'daily', 'weekly', 'monthly', 'hourly' for time-based; 'static' for a fixed set of values (e.g. customers); 'multi' for date × static (e.g. day × customer). Leave empty for unpartitioned.
partition_type.label: Partition Type

partition_cron_schedule.label: Partition Cron Schedule
partition_cron_schedule.description: Required when partition_type='cron'. A cron expression restricting the date axis to a custom cadence, e.g. '0 0 * * 1-5' for weekdays only (business-day cadence). Built on Dagster's TimeWindowPartitionsDefinition(cron_schedule=...).

partition_cron_fmt.label: Partition Cron Fmt
partition_cron_fmt.description: strftime format for partition keys produced by partition_type='cron'. Only change this for a sub-daily cron_schedule.

partition_end_offset.label: Partition End Offset
partition_end_offset.description: Passed through to the underlying Daily/Weekly/Monthly/Hourly/cron partitions definition. 0 (the Dagster default) means a time-based partition set only ever holds COMPLETED windows -- e.g. a daily set never includes today until tomorrow. Set to 1 to include the current, still-in-progress window.

partition_timezone.label: Partition Timezone
partition_timezone.description: IANA timezone for the underlying Daily/Weekly/Monthly/Hourly/cron partitions definition (defaults to UTC when unset, matching Dagster's own default).

backfill_policy.label: Backfill Policy
backfill_policy.description: Backfill execution strategy for a partitioned asset. 'single_run' materializes an entire backfill range in one run. 'multi_run' launches one run per partition (optionally capped via backfill_policy_max_partitions_per_run). Leave unset for Dagster's default (one run per partition, uncapped). Ignored when partition_type is not set.

backfill_policy_max_partitions_per_run.label: Backfill Policy Max Partitions Per Run
backfill_policy_max_partitions_per_run.description: For backfill_policy='multi_run' only: maximum partitions materialized per run. Leave unset for Dagster's default (1 partition per run).

partition_start.description: ISO date string for the first partition, e.g. '2024-01-01'. Required for time-based and multi partition types.
partition_start.label: Partition Start Date

partition_values.description: Comma-separated values for static or multi partitioning, e.g. 'acme_corp,globex,initech'. Required for static and multi types.
partition_values.label: Partition Values

partition_dimensions.description: Multi-axis partition spec: list of {name, type, start, values, dynamic_partition_name} dicts. Overrides flat fields when set.
partition_dimensions.label: Partition Dimensions

retry_policy_max_retries.description: Max retries on asset failure. Defines a RetryPolicy. Useful for transient network failures, rate limits, etc.
retry_policy_max_retries.label: Retry Policy Max Retries

column_lineage.label: Column Lineage
column_lineage.description: Column-level lineage, emitted as `dagster/column_lineage` metadata on every materialization: {output column: [upstream columns]}, e.g. {'chunk_text': ['content']}. The upstream asset is `upstream_asset_key`, or the only entry of `deps`; with several upstream assets, name each column '<asset_key>:<column>'. Ignored with a warning when no upstream asset can be resolved.

skip_unchanged.label: Skip Unchanged
skip_unchanged.description: Persist a per-URL {etag, last_modified, content_hash} fingerprint to state_path between runs. On the next run, each known URL is fetched with If-None-Match/If-Modified-Since from its stored etag/last_modified; a 304 response (or, failing that, an unchanged content_hash after a real fetch) reuses the cached row instead of reparsing -- the output still covers every page every run, just without the redundant parse work for pages that haven't changed. Off by default: every page is refetched and reparsed unconditionally, matching this component's original behavior.

state_path.label: State Path
state_path.description: Where skip_unchanged persists its per-URL fingerprint state (a JSON file). Defaults to './{asset_name}_crawler_state.json'. Ignored when skip_unchanged=False.

write_disposition.label: Write Disposition
write_disposition.description: dlt write disposition for the destination table. 'replace' (default): each run's crawl fully replaces the table. dlt's own default is 'append', which has no notion of a previous crawl's pages becoming stale -- every re-run keeps adding another full copy of every page on top of the last (a real, previously-shipped bug: row_count doubled on every rerun of an unchanged site, with no way to tell the loads apart downstream). 'merge': upserts keyed on `doc_id` (the page URL) -- keeps pages from a prior run that this run's crawl didn't revisit (e.g. max_pages capped this run short), unlike 'replace' which drops them. 'append': the old behavior, kept as an explicit opt-in for anyone who deliberately wants a historical log of every crawl rather than current-state pages.

strip_boilerplate.label: Strip Boilerplate
strip_boilerplate.description: Drop page chrome before it reaches extraction: <nav>/<header>/<footer>/<aside> tags and role='navigation'/'banner'/'contentinfo' elements are removed, and when the page has a <main> or <article> tag, only ITS text is kept (not the rest of <body>). On top of that, any line that repeats across a wide fraction of this run's pages (e.g. a 'Sign in' link or a promo banner baked into every page's template, with no semantic landmark tag to catch structurally) is dropped from every page it appears on -- a real production issue: crawled pages without this turned entity extraction's navigation/footer text into nonsense "entities" like "Tags"/"page"/"banner". Set False to restore raw full-page text. Run metadata reports `removed_chars`.
